# ExportPlan

Namespace `Nfty.Core.Publish` in assembly `Nfty.Core`.

```csharp
public record ExportPlan
```

Everything an export will contain, worked out without writing anything.

## Remarks

**This exists so the sentence a user reads before pressing Export is generated by the code that does the exporting.** The alternative — a front-end assembling its own summary from the same checkboxes — is how a screen comes to promise one thing and ship another, and shipping something other than what the screen promised is precisely the defect this whole feature exists to prevent.

### DialogWarnings { #p-dialogwarnings }

```csharp
public IReadOnlyList<string> DialogWarnings { get; init; }
```

The same warnings, in the same order, worded for the export dialog: they name its fields ("Image base URI") where [`ExportPlan.Warnings`](Nfty.Core.Publish.ExportPlan.md#p-warnings) names the command-line flags.

**Remarks**

Core owns both wordings so the two front-ends cannot disagree about WHICH warnings apply, only about what to call the control that fixes them. Empty only when [`ExportPlan.Warnings`](Nfty.Core.Publish.ExportPlan.md#p-warnings) is.

### SpriteSheet { #p-spritesheet }

```csharp
public SpriteSheetLayout? SpriteSheet { get; init; }
```

The sheet this export will stitch, or null when it is not making one.

**Remarks**

**The one part of an export that does not exist yet.** Every [`ExportEntry`](Nfty.Core.Publish.ExportEntry.md) names a file on disk and carries its real size; a sheet is built BY the export, so at plan time there is a grid and a pixel size and no bytes. It is described here rather than left out of the plan, because the plan is what the screen promises and a sheet that appeared in the output without appearing in the list is exactly the defect this seam exists to prevent. The plan [`ExportResult`](Nfty.Core.Publish.ExportResult.md) carries has it as an ordinary entry, with its real size.

### Warnings { #p-warnings }

```csharp
public IReadOnlyList<string> Warnings { get; init; }
```

Things true of this export that its author should hear before uploading it — dangling image links, links still relative — worded here so the terminal and the dialog say the same thing.

**Remarks**

Warnings, never refusals: each describes an export that is legitimate for SOME destination (a folder of art uploaded separately, say).

## Methods

### Parts() { #m-parts }

```csharp
public IReadOnlyList<string> Parts();
```

What is going, one line per part — `images/ 500 files`, `set.json`, `ChestDemo.cbk`.

**Returns.** The lines, in `Ordinal` order.

**Remarks**

**Named, not counted, and rendered here rather than in each front-end.** "Exported 1,502 files" is exactly the sentence that let a packed Set carry its author's source book without anyone noticing; a reader checks a list of four things and does not check a number. Core renders it for the reason the reports in `Stats/` are rendered here — the terminal and the dialog have to say the identical thing, not something similar.
